<action type="say">
I’m not able to see any credit card on your profile in this environment, so I can’t directly submit the lost-card report for you. You should still treat this as urgent.

Here’s exactly what to do right now:

1. **Contact your card issuer immediately**
   - Call the number on the back of the card (if you have a photo/old statement) or search “[your bank name] lost credit card phone number.”
   - When you reach them, say something like:  
     “I need to report my credit card as **lost**, not stolen. It’s my main card and the only credit card on my account. The last time I’m sure I had it was **Saturday afternoon at the grocery store**. Please **block it immediately and issue a replacement card**.”

2. **Ask them to confirm**
   - That the **current card is blocked** and **cannot be used again**.
   - That a **replacement card is being issued**, and:
     - When it will arrive.
     - Whether the **card number will change**.
     - Whether any **recurring payments/autopays** will be transferred automatically.

3. **Check for unauthorized transactions**
   - Log in to your bank/credit card app or website.
   - Review transactions from **Saturday to today**.
   - If you see anything you don’t recognize, tell the bank you want to **dispute those transactions** as part of the same call.

4. **After the call**
   - Write down:
     - Time of your call
     - Name/ID of the representative
     - Any **case or reference number**
   - Once the replacement arrives, update:
     - Any **online accounts** (streaming, subscriptions, utilities, phone, etc.)
     - Any **mobile wallets** (Apple Pay, Google Pay, etc.)

If you tell me your bank’s name, I can draft a very short script specific to that bank for you to read when you call or chat with them.</action>
